description: Claims about three open-access papers (CC BY 4.0, see ../fulltext/README.md). Gold policy: a finding stated in the methods, results or discussion is supported; background found only in the abstract or introduction (prior work, motivation) is partially_supported; anything absent or contradicted is unsupported. Labelled by the implementer from the papers; needs human review.

pairs.claim: Morning resistance training produced similar ratings of perceived exertion in the nap and no-nap conditions.
pairs.label: supported

pairs.claim: Athletes reported napping for about 35 minutes on average.
pairs.label: supported

pairs.claim: Sleep on the night before each trial did not differ between the nap and control conditions.
pairs.label: supported

pairs.claim: Napping did not change reaction time.
pairs.label: supported

pairs.claim: Mean power output in the fixed-intensity cycling session did not differ between the nap and control conditions.
pairs.label: supported

pairs.claim: Whether athletes actually slept was self-reported and was not confirmed with polysomnography.
pairs.label: supported

pairs.claim: The nap increased afternoon peak power output.
pairs.label: supported

pairs.claim: Insufficient sleep impairs physical performance, mood and cognitive function.
pairs.label: partially_supported

pairs.claim: In elite karate athletes, a 30-minute nap improved cognitive outcomes.
pairs.label: partially_supported

pairs.claim: Professional rugby athletes sleep about six and a half hours per night on average.
pairs.label: partially_supported

pairs.claim: Most professional rugby athletes report napping on match days.
pairs.label: partially_supported

pairs.claim: Daytime naps are commonly used by elite athletes.
pairs.label: partially_supported

pairs.claim: The nap improved afternoon reaction time.
pairs.label: unsupported

pairs.claim: Napping increased total sleep time on the following night.
pairs.label: unsupported

pairs.claim: Caffeine taken before the nap enhanced its effect on sprint performance.
pairs.label: unsupported

pairs.claim: Female athletes benefited more from napping than male athletes.
pairs.label: unsupported

pairs.claim: All participants in the study were male trained swimmers.
pairs.label: supported

pairs.claim: The protein group drank whey protein isolate about 30 minutes before bedtime.
pairs.label: supported

pairs.claim: Peak oxygen uptake improved over the two weeks of training in both groups.
pairs.label: supported

pairs.claim: Pre-sleep whey protein did not reduce blood markers of muscle damage.

pairs.claim: Most participants could not tell which supplement they had consumed.
pairs.label: supported

pairs.claim: The study was double-blind.
pairs.label: supported

pairs.claim: Blood samples were analysed for interleukin-6, interleukin-10 and tumour necrosis factor alpha.
pairs.label: supported

pairs.claim: Sprint interval training sessions usually consist of 4 to 12 all-out efforts lasting about 10 to 30 seconds.
pairs.label: partially_supported

pairs.claim: Protein taken before sleep increases overnight plasma amino acid availability and muscle protein synthesis.
pairs.label: partially_supported

pairs.claim: Whey and casein taken before sleep produce similar muscle protein synthesis.
pairs.label: partially_supported

pairs.claim: Pre-sleep protein can improve overnight muscle recovery after exercise-induced muscle damage.

pairs.claim: Pre-sleep protein supplementation improved 200-m swimming performance.

pairs.claim: The study included both male and female swimmers.

pairs.claim: Casein was used as the protein supplement.
pairs.label: unsupported

pairs.claim: Participants in the protein group slept significantly longer.
pairs.label: unsupported

pairs.claim: VerifiAgent was evaluated on GSM8K and MATH for mathematical reasoning.
pairs.label: supported

pairs.claim: On the ReWild hybrid reasoning dataset, VerifiAgent achieved the best accuracy of 0.78.
pairs.label: supported

pairs.claim: By default, both the reasoner and VerifiAgent used GPT-4o as their backbone model.
pairs.label: supported

pairs.claim: The Backward Verifier masks a condition of the question and asks the model to predict it.
pairs.label: supported

pairs.claim: Inference scaling with VerifiAgent outperformed majority voting while using fewer samples.
pairs.label: supported

pairs.claim: When the reasoner is stronger than VerifiAgent's backbone, adding VerifiAgent gives only a limited gain.
pairs.label: supported
